correctness.rationale: A shared one-coordinate gives at most four differing reads, hence admissible supports are disjoint. For two disjoint supports the number of differing reads is eight minus the number of cycle edges internal to their four occupied coordinates. Among k disjoint supports there are at least 4k−n fully occupied edges, and at most binomial(k,2) for k≥3: there is at most one transition per unordered label pair; an internal occupied edge isolates its label from any other, so that case gives at most 1+binomial(k−1,2). These exclude three words at n=7,8 and four at n=9. The same edge count for four points or the bound d_p≤n proves the shorter exclusions; the small witnesses satisfy the ordered-pair threshold. For n=2k≥10 every occupied position in the tour construction has a unique label, and a simple 4-regular connected graph's tour uses each label twice. Inserting a common zero destroys, but cannot create, occupied adjacencies. Conversely at even equality the entire cycle is occupied; a loop would have an adjacent edge to another label, and repeated undirected edges would violate the two-label condition. Thus the sequence gives a connected simple 4-regular graph and an Euler circuit. Independently encoded each read as 2x_i+x_{i+1} and used exact compatibility-clique recursion max(C(S−v),1+C((S−v)∩N(v))); this gave 1,1,1,1,1,2,2,3,5 for n=2 through 10. The proof is unbounded; the frozen verification report and script were inspected, not rerun.

For n≥7 pair-weight four permits either two nonadjacent ones or three consecutive ones. At d_p≥7 two active-read sets of size four intersect in at most one, so their one-supports are disjoint. Deleting the middle one of a run of three preserves its active-read set and still leaves disjoint support, hence preserves the distance in that code. The reverse equality of optimal sizes follows from nonadjacent weight-two witnesses: {0,2},{4,6} at n=7,8, the stated n=9 witness, and the tours thereafter.

A full prior exact pair-weight-four function would therefore cover the size formula; the accessible abstract alone cannot resolve that.
